prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1176; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver was named on the policy as a person who may NOT drive the car.
text:
Entry 1: Side impact reported at an intersection. The insured vehicle was struck on the driver's side by another car. Police attended the scene and confirmed the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 2: Claimant is represented by counsel, and all contact is now routed through the attorney's office. Photos from the scene confirm some details of the collision, though no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection completed. Damage is mostly consistent with the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Reviewing the policy, the driver at the time of loss is listed as a person who is not permitted to drive the insured vehicle. Referred the matter to the coverage team for review before any further decision is made.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a knee injury from the collision. Medical records show treatment followed a usual course and eased off as the patient improved. No earlier injury to the same area is known, but it is not yet clear whether this crash caused the injury.

Entry 6: Claimant's account has been taken again through counsel. Some small details were added since the first statement, but the core account has stayed the same. File remains open pending the coverage review and the medical assessment.
